request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
All 4 tests in the spec now pass under `bin/e2e`, with no build warnings or errors.

**What changed**

- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V31__person_hold_interval.sql`, adds a `person_hold` table with a required from-date and an optional to-date, and drops the old `person.held` yes/no column. Anyone who was held before gets a hold starting `0001-01-01` with no end, so their totals don't change.
- **Server:**
  - `Person` now keeps a list of holds (the new `Hold.java`). "On hold: yes/no" now means "has any hold at all".
  - A claim is left out of the live totals only when it is open, dated within one of the person's holds, and not bound by a statement. `Rollup` and `StatementService` use this rule.
  - `POST …/people/{id}/hold` takes `{from, to}`. A blank from-date uses the sheet's today, and each call adds a hold rather than switching one on or off. It writes `PERSON_HELD sheet=… by=… name=… from=<date>`. The release action and the `PERSON_RELEASED` record are gone.
- **Front end:** each person's row has "Hold from" and "to" date fields, a Hold button, and one line per hold (`person-hold-line`). The live totals in the browser use the same rule as the server. Changing a hold date clears an earlier hold error on that row.

**Three decisions you may want to check** (the test doesn't cover any of them):

1. **PENDING claims are treated as open.** The old code left PENDING claims out of a held person's totals, and the rest of the app already treats PENDING as still open, so a PENDING claim dated within a hold is also left out. The request says only "OPEN", so if you meant that strictly, it's a one-line change in `Person.heldOn` and `countsWithHolds`.
2. **A new statement ignores the old binding.** When a statement is taken, an open claim dated within a hold counts as excluded even if the previous statement bound it. So a new statement can unbind that claim, and it then drops out of the totals.
3. **A to-date before the from-date is refused.** The request doesn't say what to do here. Such a hold shows the row's error and saves nothing to the store or the audit file.
